newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA TO ISSUE SIX-MONTH T-BILLS IN AUGUST.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA TO ISSUE SIX-MONTH T-BILLS IN AUGUST.

text.p: Romania's Finance Ministry, seeking to consolidate internal public debt, will launch two issues of six-month treasury bills next month, an official said.

"There will be issues of discount T-bills which we hope will stimulate trading on the secondary market," Mihai Tanasescu, general manager of the ministry public debt department, told Reuters on Thursday.
Apart from 1.172 trillion lei worth of 182-day T-bills, the ministry will also launch next month an issue of 82.05 billion lei in three-month bills, he said.

Last August, Romania launched its first dollar-denominated domestic issue of T-bills with one-year maturity. The ministry has since used only leu-denominated paper for three months to cover a part of the country's bulging budget deficit.
Tanasescu said the ministry did not plan to issue rollover paper to cover the $104.8 million worth of dollar-denominated bonds due to mature on August 15.
All T-bills to be issued next month have a face value of 10 million lei and will be offered through a single-price (Dutch-style) auction, at competitive bids.
Auctions are scheduled two days before issue date.
Under the current rules, the bills are available for commercial banks operating in Romania and their Romanian resident corporate clients.
At the latest auction, the yield fell to 25 percent from a previous 34 percent following oversubscription amid a liquid money market.
